claims.text: The untreated as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a predominantly FCC plus ordered B2 dual-phase lamellar structure.
A Zr concentration of x=0.05 corresponds to approximately 5 atomic percent Zr.
Adding approximately 5 atomic percent Zr to as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will improve mechanical durability relative to the Zr-free alloy.
Adding approximately 5 atomic percent Zr will improve room-temperature creep resistance relative to the Zr-free alloy.
Adding approximately 5 atomic percent Zr will maintain acceptable corrosion resistance relative to the Zr-free alloy.
The x=0.05 Zr addition induces lattice distortion in the FCC/B2 matrix.
The x=0.05 Zr addition promotes fine semi-coherent or coherent Ni7Zr2 precipitates.
The Ni7Zr2 precipitates are dispersed or form a discontinuous network bridging the FCC and B2 phases.
Zr-induced lattice distortion and Ni7Zr2 precipitation impede dislocation motion.
Zr-induced lattice distortion and Ni7Zr2 precipitation impede grain-boundary sliding and thereby reduce creep.
The proposed lattice-distortion and precipitation-strengthening mechanisms increase yield strength and compressive strength.
A passivating film potentially containing ZrO2 provides corrosion protection at the moderate Zr addition.
Higher Zr content produces a more continuous Zr-rich phase and better corrosion resistance.
The x=0.05 alloy will have significantly higher hardness, yield strength, and compressive strength than the x=0 alloy.
The x=0.05 alloy will have less room-temperature creep deformation than the x=0 alloy.
The x=0.05 alloy will have better corrosion resistance than x=0 but poorer corrosion resistance than x=0.1.
An x=0.1 Zr addition compromises mechanical performance relative to x=0.05.
The untreated alloy is approximately 70% FCC.
The untreated alloy has an approximate yield strength of 705 MPa and compressive strength of 1183 MPa.
The untreated alloy has a corrosion current density of approximately 0.09993 μA/cm2 and a pitting potential of approximately 320 mV under the stated corrosion-test regime.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis equates x=0.05 with approximately 5 atomic percent Zr, but if x denotes the added stoichiometric coefficient in AlCoCrFeNi2.1Zrx, x=0.05 corresponds to only about 0.81 atomic percent Zr. The notation must be defined as an atomic fraction rather than a formula coefficient for the stated equivalence to hold.
